rows.facility_bundling_rule: Cigna bundles routine facility services and room-and-board; denies separate reimbursement for incidental items.
Facility services are DRG/case-rate bundled, with no separate reimbursement for related 30-day readmissions.
Generally bundled for facility claims with room/facility fees; Wisconsin allows separate reimbursement.
Facility observation monitoring for chemotherapy is bundled into chemotherapy; no separate reporting.
Inpatient and outpatient facility claims are bundled into room and board or primary service charges.
Routine, integral facility and infusion services are bundled into facility or administration charges.

reimbursement_policies.evidence: The policy does not name this chemotherapy DRG pattern or create a Wisconsin- or facility-specific inpatient chemotherapy episode rule. However, it applies general facility bundling rules that are relevant to inpatient chemotherapy claims: routine nursing, room and board, supplies, equipment, and many injection/infusion administration services are included in facility reimbursement, and chemotherapy administration work in the facility setting is described as routine nursing rather than separately reportable physician work. A limited exception states that administration services associated with an infusion or injection may be separately reimbursed when the infusion/injection is the primary reason for the facility visit.

provider_role_restrictions: physician reporting not intended in facility

reimbursement_policies.evidence: Inpatient and facility-based infusion or chemotherapy administration services are bundled into the primary medical/surgical payment or treated as incidental. Routine inpatient supplies, equipment, and administration charges are not separately reimbursed.

pairing_conditions: CMS-1500 with facility place of service

reimbursement_policies.evidence: This is a general inpatient readmission reimbursement policy, not a chemotherapy-DRG-specific policy. The requested chemotherapy pattern is not named, and admissions for the medical treatment of cancer are explicitly excluded from the readmission denial rule. The policy also states that planned readmissions and/or leave-of-absence readmissions within 30 days are treated as one admission with one DRG reimbursed.

exemptions: transfers from one facility to another

reasons: relevance judge: relevant=false confidence='medium': This is a general inpatient readmission policy, but the pattern is for inpatient chemotherapy episodes; the policy does not target chemotherapy DRGs and explicitly excludes admissions for medical treatment of cancer from the readmission denial rule.

reimbursement_policies.evidence: For facility claims, chemotherapy administration and infusion drug administration are treated as bundled or integral to the facility fee and are not separately reimbursed when billed on the same date of service as a room or facility fee. Stand-alone always-bundled items are denied, and modifiers do not override those denials.

pairing_conditions: same claim with room or facility fee
exemptions: provider, state, federal contract, and/or requirements

reimbursement_policies.evidence: Facility claims for chemotherapy administration are generally bundled with the room or facility fee and not separately reimbursable, but Wisconsin permits separate reimbursement for chemotherapy administration and infusion administration.

pairing_conditions: same claim as room or facility fee
state_specific_rules: WI: chemotherapy administration and infusion administration may be separately reimbursed

reimbursement_policies.evidence: Off-topic for inpatient DRG chemotherapy. The policy is limited to office-based injection and infusion reimbursement and does not set a DRG payment rule.

Medica reimburses facility observation services only when billed under observation rules, up to 48 hours and only after at least 8 hours are reported. Observation used for monitoring associated with chemotherapy is not separately reimbursable because it is considered part of the procedure.

Routine facility supplies and services used in hospital care are bundled into the room, board, accommodation, or procedure charge and are not separately reimbursable when they are integral to the service delivered.

reimbursement_policies.policy_title: Outpatient Hospital Services Rendered Prior to an Inpatient Admission
reimbursement_policies.evidence: The policy is not chemotherapy-specific, but it governs inpatient admission claims that may include outpatient services before admission. Outpatient diagnostic services within the 3-day or 1-day window are bundled into the inpatient payment. Related outpatient nondiagnostic services in that window are also bundled, while unrelated services or services outside the window may be billed separately.

reimbursement_policies.policy_title: RM-042 Facility Routine Services, Supplies and Medical Equipment\
reimbursement_policies.evidence: Chemotherapy administration is treated as an incremental nursing/ancillary service included in facility reimbursement and not separately billable when routine or included in another service charge.

recommended_action.description:
Recommendation 1: CA EPO: bundle/deny separate facility reimbursement for 96401, 96402, 96409-96425, 96360-96379, and 96521-96523 when performed in facility setting and reported on UB04 or CMS-1500 with facility place of service with the primary medical/surgical service; allow separate payment only when infusion/injection is the primary reason for visit or when revenue code 0230-0239 has a physician order and documentation. Apply to CA. Exempt: infusion/injection primary reason for visit, 0230-0239 with physician order and documentation. Peer: Cigna and Providence Health Plan both treat revenue code 0230-0239 as facility-bundled, with same-date/same-claim facility guardrails..

Recommendation 2: CA EPO: bundle G0498 on the same date of service when billed on the same claim as room or facility fee by a facility provider, and keep the separately reimbursed chemotherapy/infusion administration carve-out limited to Wisconsin only. Apply to CA. Exempt: Wisconsin: chemotherapy administration, Wisconsin: infusion administration. Peer: Elevance Health (external) and Elevance Health (internal) both bundle G0498 on the same date of service when it is on the same claim as a room or facility fee..
